title: Multi-Cluster Management, Cluster API (CAPI), vCluster & Cilium ClusterMesh
summary: Master enterprise multi-cluster orchestration, declarative fleet management, and hybrid mesh topologies: provisioning clusters declaratively with Cluster API (CAPI Cluster, MachineDeployment, and AWSCluster/AzureCluster infrastructure providers), provisioning lightweight virtual tenant clusters using vCluster, and configuring cross-cluster service discovery with Cilium ClusterMesh and MCS (Multi-Cluster Services) ServiceExport/ServiceImport.
learningObjectives: Declare and deploy Kubernetes clusters as first-class resources using Cluster API (CAPI) Cluster and MachineDeployment manifests.
Architect multi-tenant virtual control planes using vCluster to achieve tenant isolation while sharing underlying physical nodes.
Implement cross-cluster service mesh networking and global DNS discovery with Cilium ClusterMesh and Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) ServiceImport/ServiceExport.

curriculumModules.title: Declarative Fleet Lifecycle with Cluster API (CAPI)
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Cluster API (CAPI) treats Kubernetes clusters and worker node machines as declarative Kubernetes resources. A management cluster uses CustomResourceDefinitions (Cluster, MachineDeployment, ControlPlane, and Infrastructure Providers like CAPA/CAPZ) to provision, upgrade, and reconcile workload clusters across heterogeneous clouds and bare-metal environments.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Adopt a GitOps-driven management cluster pattern where platform teams manage fleet-wide Kubernetes version upgrades and OS patching via Git pull requests updating MachineDeployment version fields.

curriculumModules.title: Virtual Clusters (vCluster) & Cilium ClusterMesh with MCS
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: To prevent physical cluster sprawl, vCluster creates isolated virtual Kubernetes control planes inside namespaces of an underlying host cluster, giving tenants full admin access (CRDs, namespaces) without multi-cluster overhead. Across physical clusters, Cilium ClusterMesh connects eBPF routing engines without ingress gateways, enabling seamless pod-to-pod cross-cluster routing and Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) ServiceExport/ServiceImport resolution.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Utilize vCluster for multi-tenant dev/staging sandbox environments and link production regional clusters via Cilium ClusterMesh with MCS ServiceImports for zero-egress cross-region disaster recovery.

labs.title: Provisioning Declarative Workload Clusters via Cluster API MachineDeployment
labs.scenario: Deploy a declarative worker fleet for a production workload cluster: author a Cluster API MachineDeployment manifest in /fleet/worker-fleet.yaml named prod-worker-fleet in namespace fleet-system with 3 replicas targeting cluster prod-cluster and version v1.32.0. Apply to namespace fleet-system.
labs.productionContext: Using CAPI MachineDeployments automates worker node rolling replacements during CVE patch cycles without manual node provisioning.
objectives: Create namespace fleet-system if not present.
Configure clusterName to prod-cluster and replicas to 3.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: MachineDeployment
metadata:
  name: prod-worker-fleet
  namespace: fleet-system
spec:
  clusterName: prod-cluster
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-name: prod-cluster
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-name: prod-cluster
    spec:
      clusterName: prod-cluster
      version: v1.32.0

steps.title: Create fleet-system namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace fleet-system if not present.

steps.title: Author MachineDeployment manifest
steps.instruction: Author manifest /fleet/worker-fleet.yaml targeting cluster prod-cluster with 3 replicas.

validationRules.description: MachineDeployment prod-worker-fleet exists in namespace fleet-system
validationRules.name: prod-worker-fleet
validationRules.remediation: Apply MachineDeployment prod-worker-fleet in namespace fleet-system

validationRules.name: prod-worker-fleet
validationRules.remediation: Set spec.clusterName: prod-cluster on MachineDeployment prod-worker-fleet

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /fleet/worker-fleet.yaml
apiVersion: cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: MachineDeployment
metadata:
  name: prod-worker-fleet
  namespace: fleet-system
spec:
  clusterName: prod-cluster
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-name: prod-cluster
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        cluster.x-k8s.io/cluster-name: prod-cluster
    spec:
      clusterName: prod-cluster
      version: v1.32.0
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: MachineDeployment missing or target cluster mismatch.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: MachineDeployment must target clusterName prod-cluster in namespace fleet-system.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Verify spec.clusterName is prod-cluster and apply to namespace fleet-system.

labs.title: Cross-Cluster Service Discovery with Cilium ClusterMesh & MCS
labs.scenario: Configure cross-cluster multi-cloud service discovery: verify multi-cluster mesh connectivity via cilium clustermesh status, author a Multi-Cluster Services ServiceImport manifest in /fleet/checkout-service-import.yaml named checkout-service in namespace production of type ClusterSetIP targeting port 8080. Apply to namespace production.
labs.productionContext: Multi-Cluster Services (MCS) ServiceImports allow pods in one cluster to discover and communicate with services in another cluster using standard DNS names (service.namespace.svc.clusterset.local).
objectives: Audit ClusterMesh connectivity via cilium clustermesh status.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: multicluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceImport
metadata:
  name: checkout-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  type: ClusterSetIP
  ports:
    - port: 8080
      protocol: TCP

steps.title: Verify ClusterMesh status
steps.instruction: Execute cilium clustermesh status to verify cross-cluster tunnel synchronization.

steps.title: Author ServiceImport manifest
steps.instruction: Author manifest /fleet/checkout-service-import.yaml for checkout-service of type ClusterSetIP.

steps.title: Apply ServiceImport
steps.instruction: Apply ServiceImport manifest to namespace production.

validationRules.description: ServiceImport checkout-service exists in namespace production
validationRules.name: checkout-service
validationRules.remediation: Apply ServiceImport checkout-service in namespace production

validationRules.name: checkout-service
validationRules.remediation: Set spec.type: ClusterSetIP on ServiceImport checkout-service

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /fleet/checkout-service-import.yaml
apiVersion: multicluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceImport
metadata:
  name: checkout-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  type: ClusterSetIP
  ports:
    - port: 8080
      protocol: TCP
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: ServiceImport validation fails or clustermesh not checked.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: Cilium clustermesh status command must be executed and ServiceImport must be created in namespace production.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Execute cilium clustermesh status and apply /fleet/checkout-service-import.yaml to namespace production.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Cluster API (CAPI) handle automated rolling upgrades of worker nodes in a MachineDeployment?
options: It deletes all physical nodes simultaneously causing downtime.

It provisions a new Machine matching the updated MachineTemplate, waits for it to join the cluster as a Ready Node, drains old nodes safely while respecting PodDisruptionBudgets, and deletes old Machines sequentially.
It modifies the Linux kernel dynamically via SSH.
It converts worker nodes into Docker containers.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: CAPI MachineDeployments follow the Kubernetes Deployment controller model: they create a new MachineSet, scale up new Machines with the updated spec, wait for them to become Ready, cordons and drains old nodes, and scales down the old MachineSet.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Cilium ClusterMesh achieve cross-cluster service routing without dedicated ingress/egress gateway bottlenecks?
options: It routes all traffic through a single public IP in AWS.

By synchronizing cluster states via etcd/apiserver proxies and managing eBPF connection tracking maps directly in the Linux kernel, allowing pods in cluster A to route packets directly to pod IPs in cluster B over flat underlay or overlay tunnels.
It encapsulates all packets in base64 HTTP requests.
It relies exclusively on DNS round-robin without health checking.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Cilium ClusterMesh establishes direct pod-to-pod networking across clusters using eBPF datapath routing and distributed mesh state synchronization, eliminating the latency and cost of intermediate edge gateways.
